name: Lot's wife
charge: Looking back toward Sodom against the angel's command
summary: The angels told Lot's household to escape for their lives and not look behind them. His wife looked back from behind him and became a pillar of salt. Christ made her a proverb in three words.
offense: The command was given with the rescue and it was specific: escape for thy life, look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain, escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed (Genesis 19:17). She had been taken out by the hand, along with her husband and her two daughters, the Lord being merciful unto them (Genesis 19:16), so mercy had already brought her beyond the city's walls. The command required her to continue the escape, neither looking back nor remaining in the plain. What the city she was leaving had become is set out in the same chapter. The men of Sodom compassed the house, both old and young, all the people from every quarter, and demanded the two men, saying, bring them out unto us, that we may know them (Genesis 19:4-5). To know in scripture is to lie with: Adam knew Eve his wife, and she conceived (Genesis 4:1), and Rebekah was a virgin, neither had any man known her (Genesis 24:16). So the demand was that the guests be handed over to be raped, by the whole male population of the city, and Lot's own answer, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly (Genesis 19:7),  shows this was already wickedness in Genesis, long before the law was written at Sinai, where it is named abomination (Leviticus 18:22). The same demand in the same words is made at Gibeah by certain sons of Belial, bring forth the man that came into thine house, that we may know him (Judges 19:22), and Jude names what the cities were doing, giving themselves over to fornication and going after strange flesh (Jude 1:7).
judgment: She looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:26). The account records no further warning between the backward look and its consequence. Christ raises her case by name as a warning to those who will turn back on the day of his revealing, in the day when he which shall be upon the housetop and his stuff in the house is told not to come down to take it away: Remember Lot's wife (Luke 17:31-32). Wisdom keeps the standing pillar as a memorial of an unbelieving soul (Wisdom of Solomon 10:7). Christ places the warning beside the temptation to return for possessions and the effort to save one's life only to lose it (Luke 17:31-33). Being led out was not the end of obedience. Her case warns against turning back after deliverance has begun, without requiring an invented account of what she was thinking when she looked.

verses.text: And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed.
But his wife looked back from behind him, and she became a pillar of salt.
In that day, he which shall be upon the housetop, and his stuff in the house, let him not come down to take it away: and he that is in the field, let him likewise not return back.
Whosoever shall seek to save his life shall lose it; and whosoever shall lose his life shall preserve it.

Of whose wickedness even to this day the waste land that smoketh is a testimony, and plants bearing fruit that never come to ripeness: and a standing pillar of salt is a monument of an unbelieving soul.

lawDetails.text: You shall obey the voice of the LORD your God.

entries.commentary: Lot sat in the gate and pressed the two angels into his house, because he knew the men of Sodom. He made them a feast, and they did eat; angels have bodies and functions like men.

The men of Sodom, old and young, all the people from every quarter, compassed the house and demanded the men, that we may know them. To know in scripture is to lie with: Rebekah was a virgin, neither had any man known her. The whole city, both small and great, was given to this wickedness.

Lot went out and said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. This is Genesis, way before [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18); sodomy was already wickedness and already unlawful before the law was written at Sinai. They pressed on Lot to break the door, and the angels smote them with blindness, small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

Lot's sons in law took him as one that mocked, and they perished. When the warning comes, treating it as a joke is death. While Lot lingered, the angels laid hold on his hand, the Lord being merciful to him. Then the instruction: Escape for thy life; look not behind thee; escape to the mountain.

The angel told Lot, Haste thee, for I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither. The destruction waited on the righteous being brought out, the same way the angels in [Revelation 7](/bible/revelation/7) hold the four winds until the servants of God are sealed. When Lot entered Zoar, the Lord rained brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. Those cities are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire; what was done there on a small scale is done in spiritual Sodom on a greater scale, and the example stands. Just Lot was delivered, a righteous man vexed from day to day with the filthy conversation and unlawful deeds of the wicked. A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct.

Lot's wife looked back, against the instruction, and became a pillar of salt: a standing monument of an unbelieving soul. Remember Lot's wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures. As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot's wife.

Lot's daughters thought Sodom had been the whole world and no man was left on the earth to give them seed, so they made their father drink wine and lay with him; he perceived not when they lay down nor when they arose. Do not take any wayward idea from this: uncovering the nakedness of thy father is against the laws of the Most High. It was unlawful then and it is unlawful now. The firstborn bare Moab, father of the Moabites, and the younger bare Benammi, father of the Ammonites, unto this day. In this teaching those nations are identified with the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese.

lawsResolved.text: You shall obey the voice of the LORD your God.
No man, having put his hand to the plow (to follow and serve God), and then looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
God is angered at those who turn their heart from Him.
